title: AI Governance Positions, 2026
method: Descriptive coding of documented public positions. No actor is ranked or scored. Empty or qualified fields mean the available sources do not support a stronger claim.

actors.pace: Supports coordinated pacing when safeguards lag; temporarily slowed scaling in August 2026.
actors.governance_model: Mandatory capability-based national safety requirements plus state action, incident reporting, external expert input and company preparedness controls.
actors.independent_evaluation: Explicitly supports stronger independent safety assessments and external input.
actors.international_coordination: Supports broader coordination; says no company, industry or government can meet the challenge alone.
actors.human_control: Human supervision, blocking evaluations, trajectory monitoring and containment.
actors.openness_or_equity: Frames AGI as needing democratic governance and broad public voice.

actors.pace: Argues for pacing and coordination as capabilities approach recursive self-improvement; says unilateral pause by one lab is insufficient.
actors.governance_model: Risk-scaled regulatory ladder: transparency now, stronger external testing and incident reporting as capabilities rise, deeper government oversight at highest risk.
actors.independent_evaluation: Strong support for external testing and deeper oversight.
actors.international_coordination: Calls for broader deliberation and coordination involving policymakers, labs, researchers and civil society.
actors.human_control: Explicit concern that AI building its own successors could reduce human control.
actors.openness_or_equity: Supports benefits of development while distinguishing lower-risk open weights from dangerous-capability models.

actors.pace: Musk has publicly backed calls for coordinated slowing of frontier development; xAI continues model development under its Frontier AI Framework.
actors.governance_model: Company frontier-risk framework covering catastrophic misuse and loss of control; Musk has also supported broader coordinated caution.
actors.independent_evaluation: Framework emphasizes evaluation and safety procedures; public slowdown advocacy points to broader coordination.
actors.international_coordination: Publicly aligned with calls for cross-lab caution.
actors.human_control: Loss-of-control risk is explicitly within xAI's framework.
actors.openness_or_equity: Not the central emphasis in the sources used here.

actors.pace: Continued rapid development with internal scaling safeguards; Zuckerberg has opposed a coordinated industry slowdown.
actors.governance_model: Company-led Advanced AI Scaling Framework, deployment testing and preparedness reporting; favors competition/liability and company responsibility over a broad coordinated slowdown.
actors.independent_evaluation: Supports evaluation; recent public stance does not center mandatory external regulation.
actors.international_coordination: Participates in standards and EU transparency mechanisms, but not in a coordinated slowdown.
actors.human_control: Framework tests greater autonomy and whether surrounding controls work as intended.
actors.openness_or_equity: Strong emphasis on broad access, openness and individual empowerment through personal superintelligence.

actors.pace: Supports continued development with stronger coordination and caution around frontier capabilities; recent reporting places Hassabis among leaders sympathetic to coordinated pacing.
actors.governance_model: Responsible development combined with government, academia and civil-society partnerships.
actors.independent_evaluation: Supports safety and responsibility; the sources here do not establish a singular preferred external-audit regime.
actors.international_coordination: Strong emphasis on national and international partnerships.
actors.human_control: Responsible development for human benefit; research explicitly examines ASI emerging from multi-agent collectives.

actors.actor: Microsoft AI / Mustafa Suleyman and Satya Nadella
actors.pace: Advance frontier systems, but with explicit willingness to prioritize human control and safety over maximal autonomy.
actors.governance_model: Humanist code plus organizational governance/security controls; Suleyman supports industry standards and government oversight.
actors.independent_evaluation: Supports practical testing and oversight; recent reporting says Suleyman favors embedded independent evaluation.
actors.international_coordination: Supports a public-interest debate and standards, but does not propose one single global regime in the cited primary materials.
actors.human_control: Central principle: people matter more than AI; AI should remain subordinate to human interests.
actors.openness_or_equity: Human agency and economic opportunity emphasized.

actors.pace: Opposes regulating hypothetical harms in ways that slow an early technology; argues that advancing the technology can itself improve safety.
actors.governance_model: Company responsibility plus use of existing sectoral regulators and regulation of concrete harms rather than new broad AI-specific restrictions.
actors.independent_evaluation: Not the central governance mechanism in the cited statements.
actors.international_coordination: Engages governments and G20; emphasis is precise regulation rather than coordinated slowdown.
actors.human_control: Safety through better engineering and responsible company development.
actors.openness_or_equity: Not the central emphasis in the cited statements.

actors.pace: Supports continued development, not an industry-wide slowdown.
actors.governance_model: Rigorous testing and safeguards with industry-government collaboration.
actors.independent_evaluation: Supports rigorous testing; public reporting cited here does not specify one mandatory oversight structure.
actors.international_coordination: Supports collaboration between industry and government.
actors.human_control: Safety controls around deployment rather than a claim about AI personhood.
actors.openness_or_equity: Multi-model customer choice and enterprise controls are central to AWS deployment framing.

actors.pace: Does not argue that AI should stop; argues the trajectory must be deliberately shaped so benefits outweigh harms.
actors.governance_model: International oversight and public policy combined with directed investment in equitable applications.
actors.independent_evaluation: Supports governance and containment; not framed primarily as lab-level audit policy.
actors.human_control: Containment and alignment to human values are central concerns.
actors.openness_or_equity: Core emphasis: access, languages, health, education, agriculture and reducing global inequality.

actors.pace: Formal policy emphasizes rapid U.S. adoption and leadership; Trump has publicly opposed a broader slowdown tied to existential-risk warnings.
actors.governance_model: Targeted federal security/accountability rules plus partnership with industry, while opposing what the administration describes as burdensome regulation.
actors.independent_evaluation: Formal national-security policy emphasizes robustness, steerability, controllability and accountability; recent rhetoric resists a broad new safety-regulatory regime.
actors.international_coordination: Competition and U.S. leadership are primary; international diplomacy is part of the AI Action Plan.
actors.human_control: National-security directive requires clear constitutional chain of command and controllable systems.
actors.openness_or_equity: Economic growth, infrastructure and American leadership are dominant themes.

actors.actor: European Union / European Commission AI Office
actors.pace: Allows continued development under binding risk-based obligations rather than a blanket pause.
actors.governance_model: Statutory AI Act regime for general-purpose models; systemic-risk models face evaluation, risk mitigation, serious-incident reporting and cybersecurity duties.
actors.independent_evaluation: Requires model evaluation and adversarial testing for systemic-risk GPAI; enforcement by AI Office and national authorities.
actors.international_coordination: Uses a Code of Practice shaped through a multi-stakeholder process and engages internationally.
actors.human_control: EU materials explicitly include unintended control issues with autonomous GPAI as a systemic-risk example.
actors.openness_or_equity: Balances innovation with rights, safety and competitiveness.

actors.pace: Evidence-first evaluation; does not set a general commercial development pace in the cited materials.
actors.governance_model: Independent government capability testing, incident disclosure and risk measurement.
actors.independent_evaluation: This is its core institutional role.
actors.international_coordination: Supports shared understanding across governments, industry and the public.
actors.human_control: Testing focuses on whether safeguards and intended boundaries hold under permissive conditions.
actors.openness_or_equity: Public evidence and transparency are emphasized.

actors.actor: United Nations / Independent International Scientific Panel on AI
actors.pace: Does not prescribe a blanket pause in the cited report; stresses that waiting for certainty can make governance too late.
actors.governance_model: Independent scientific evidence feeding multilateral dialogue and international governance.
actors.independent_evaluation: Core emphasis on independent scientific evidence.
actors.international_coordination: Central objective through the Global Dialogue on AI Governance.
actors.human_control: Governance and reliability are explicit domains.
actors.openness_or_equity: Global inclusion and shared scientific basis are central.

actors.pace: Supports continued AI development and broad adoption, paired with safety, controllability and governance.
actors.governance_model: People-centered, sovereignty-aware, categorized/tiered risk governance, ethics across the lifecycle, and international cooperation.
actors.independent_evaluation: Not framed around Western-style external lab auditors in the cited documents; emphasizes governance ecosystems and state/international coordination.
actors.international_coordination: Strongly supports multilateral cooperation; launched WAICO and calls for a just and equitable global governance system.
actors.human_control: Official plans explicitly call for AI for good and safety/controllability.
actors.openness_or_equity: Strong emphasis on shared benefits, developing countries, open-source ecosystems and bridging the digital divide.
